wu: Music Opinions Relay: Students line up in two teams. Teacher shows a flashcard with a song title (e.g., 'Shape of You'). First student runs to the board, writes one opinion adjective (e.g., 'catchy'), runs back, tags next student who writes another (e.g., 'boring'), and so on. First team with 5 correct adjectives wins.
wuAlt: Opinion Charades: Teacher acts out a song genre (e.g., 'rock'), students guess and say 'I think it's rock because...'
Song Title Association: Teacher says a song, students shout an opinion word (e.g., 'Happy' → 'funny')
pres: Teacher projects a music review of 'Blinding Lights' by The Weeknd. Models sentences: 'I think it's amazing because the beat is cool' and 'The genre is synth-pop'. Underlines opinion adjectives (amazing, cool) and review phrases (genre, beat). Checks understanding: 'What's the genre? Why does he like it?'
presAlt: Genre Flashcard Sort: Students match flashcards (jazz, hip-hop) to definitions, then say 'I think jazz is... because...'
YouTube Review Analysis: Teacher plays a 30-second song review, students list 3 opinion words
prac: Two-Corners Debate: Label corners 'Love' and 'Hate'. Teacher plays 30 seconds of a controversial song (e.g., 'Baby Shark'). Students go to a corner, pair up, and say 'I love/hate it because...'. After 2 minutes, switch corners and repeat with a new song.
pracAlt: Opinion Dice Game: Students roll a dice (1=Love, 2=Hate, 3=Boring, etc.), say the opinion, and justify
Music Bingo: Teacher calls out opinion adjectives, students mark them on bingo cards and make sentences
ls: Song Excerpt Review: Students listen to 3 short song clips (1 min each). For each, they write: 1) Genre, 2) One opinion adjective, 3) One reason. Teacher plays clips twice, checks answers on the board.
re: Musical Opinions Freeze: Teacher plays upbeat music, students dance. When music stops, they freeze and say an opinion about the last song (e.g., 'I think it's loud!').
prod: Song Review Swap: Students write a 4-sentence review of their favorite song on a slip (genre, opinion, reason, rating). They swap with a partner, who reads it and says 'I agree/disagree because...'.
rw: Review Reading + Rating: Students read a short music review (60 words) about a Moroccan artist (e.g., Saad Lamjarred). They underline 5 genre words (e.g., ' Rai', 'pop') and write a 1-5 star rating with a reason.
st: Teacher plays 'Lah ya sahbi' by Cheb Khaled. Discuss: 'What genre is it? Is it traditional or modern?' End with: 'Today we learned to share music opinions. Thank you, class!'
g: Teacher hums a song, students guess the genre and say 'I think it's... because...'
Teams race to write opinion sentences on the board with correct 'because' clauses
Student draws a genre, others guess and say 'Is it hip-hop? I think so because...'
Roll dice to pick a song/opinion, students debate for 1 minute
diff: Fast finishers: Write a second review comparing two songs
Support: Use a sentence frame: 'I think ____ is ____ because ____'
hw: Write a 10-sentence review of a Moroccan song (genre, opinion, reason, rating)
Record a 30-second video review of a song
Find 3 music reviews online, copy 2 opinion sentences each
tip: Use local music (e.g., Gnawa, Rai) to build cultural relevance. Teens engage more when opinions connect to their world.
